page: Amazon Web Services r8in.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core using dedicated CPU allocation. It is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive enterprise workloads.

Hardware specifications omit integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions such as Amazon EBS for persistent data. The network configuration features a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps, and no discrete graphics processing units are included. Operating without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the instance is targeted at secure internal infrastructure deployments.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation makes the r8in.xlarge cost-efficient for setups where high memory capacity is required without provisioning unneeded compute cores. The absence of onboard NVMe storage represents a tradeoff, meaning workloads with extreme disk throughput requirements must account for network EBS performance limits. Typical target applications include in-memory caches, relational databases, real-time data analytics, and enterprise resource planning systems.
description: Amazon Web Services r8in.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an Intel x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled, alongside 32.0 GB of memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. The server does not include bundled local disk storage, depending entirely on remote block storage, and operates without GPU acceleration. Network connectivity provides a baseline throughput of 6 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Given its generous memory-to-vCPU ratio, the instance provides qualitative resource efficiency for memory-bound applications that require minimal compute overhead. The configuration is primarily tailored for running relational databases, in-memory caching solutions like Redis, intermediate data processing layers, and enterprise operational workloads.
